findings.title: Committed work with no estimate
findings.figure: 4 of 14 open items in KEL Sprint 9

findings.title: Past due with a status that has no standard meaning
findings.detail: Custom statuses (parked, awaiting client) can't be read as done or not done, so they don't show as overdue.

findings.title: Time logged against items missing from the work-item export
findings.detail: Worklogs point at KEL-7 and KEL-12, which are not in the Jira export (moved to another project or deleted).

findings.title: The same person paid twice for the same day
findings.figure: 6 days, 45 hours billed by each supplier
findings.detail: Rafe Lindqvist, seconded from Kelvaro to Brantoft on Thursdays and Fridays, has a full day in Kelvaro's Tempo and in Brantoft's ClickUp on the same days. Each supplier's data looks normal on its own.

findings.title: Milestone reported green while the delivery data says otherwise
findings.figure: M3 is G 6 days after its date; 5 open beta items, 2 overdue; design sign-off Stuck
findings.detail: The plan was last updated 2026-09-20 from a supplier update.

findings.title: One milestone, two dates
findings.detail: The supplier's own task moved; the client's plan didn't.

findings.title: Milestone marked complete on a supplier's stale data
findings.figure: Plan says Complete; OMB-4 is In Progress; the export is 21 days old
findings.detail: Ombreton's export was taken three weeks before the others, and the plan was updated from a call, not the data.

findings.title: Hours from someone nobody planned or assigned
findings.detail: Teo Brandt, a contractor, appears only in Harvest: not in the client's planner, not on the board, where the illustration item has no owner.

findings.title: One person, several names
findings.detail: The planner uses full names, ClickUp short names, and Ombreton's worklogs account names. No file carries an email that joins them.

findings.title: Supplier time that can't be tied to a deliverable
findings.detail: Harvest records project and task type, not board items. Only notes that repeat a board item's name can be linked; the rest can't.

findings.title: A supplier burning more than the client booked
findings.figure: Last four weeks: 751 hours logged against 570 booked (32% over)
findings.detail: Includes 105 hours from Rafe Lindqvist, who isn't booked at all, and QA logged at full time against a half-time booking.

ingestionTraps.title: Renamed columns
ingestionTraps.detail: Kelvaro's Jira says "Work item key" (2025), Ombreton's says "Issue key". Tempo says "Logged Hours" and "Work Item Key" (after August 2024).

ingestionTraps.title: Five units for time
ingestionTraps.detail: Seconds (Jira), milliseconds (ClickUp), h:mm (Hub Planner), decimal hours (Harvest, Tempo), h:mm:ss (monday).

ingestionTraps.title: Five date styles
ingestionTraps.detail: 02/Oct/26 9:00 AM (Jira), POSIX milliseconds and month-first text (ClickUp), dd/MM/yyyy (planner and plan), yyyy-MM-dd (Harvest, monday).

ingestionTraps.title: Two columns, one meaning
ingestionTraps.detail: Jira exports carry both a key (KEL-14) and a numeric id. Time tools refer to the key. "Parent" holds the parent's numeric id, not its key.

ingestionTraps.title: Repeated headers
ingestionTraps.detail: One "Log Work" column per worklog, all with the same header, as "comment;date;account;seconds".

ingestionTraps.title: A spreadsheet, not a table
ingestionTraps.detail: The monday export is .xlsx: board name, then each group as its own block with its own header row; subitems sit under their parent with a different header.

ingestionTraps.title: Names split or shortened
ingestionTraps.detail: Harvest splits First Name and Last Name; ClickUp uses short display names; Tempo and Jira use full names.
